title: Barrels and boxes
statementMd:
Tarly has two different type of items, food boxes and wine barrels. There are $*f*$ food boxes and $*w*$ wine barrels. Tarly stores them in various stacks and each stack can consist of either food boxes or wine barrels but not both. The stacks are placed in a line such that no two stacks of food boxes are together and no two stacks of wine barrels are together.

The height of a stack is defined as the number of items in the stack. Two stacks are considered different if either their heights are different or one of them contains food and other contains wine.

Jon Snow doesn't like an arrangement if any stack of wine barrels has height less than or equal to $*h*$. What is the probability that Jon Snow will like the arrangement if all arrangement are equiprobably?

Two arrangement of stacks are considered different if exists such $*i*$, that $*i*$-th stack of one arrangement is different from the $*i*$-th stack of the other arrangement.

## Input

The first line of input contains three integers $*f*$, $*w*$, $*h*$ ($0 ≤ *f*, *w*, *h* ≤ 10^{5}$) — number of food boxes, number of wine barrels and $*h*$ is as described above. It is guaranteed that he has at least one food box or at least one wine barrel.

## Output

Output the probability that Jon Snow will like the arrangement. The probability is of the form ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/cb0172a656698061aefa8eb30b2dbcd1e31f508e.png), then you need to output a single integer $*p*·*q*^{ - 1} *mod* (10^{9} + 7)$.

## Note

In the first example $*f*  =  1$, $*w* = 1$ and $*h* = 1$, there are only two possible arrangement of stacks and Jon Snow doesn't like any of them.

In the second example $*f* = 1$, $*w* = 2$ and $*h* = 1$, there are three arrangements. Jon Snow likes the (1) and (3) arrangement. So the probabilty is ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/14b21b617fcd2e25700376368355f7bbf975d8de.png).

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/ace4ab85ebe9626a851b3d4270a7dd7ed4b241c5.png)
statementZhMd:
Tarly 有两种不同类型的物品：食品箱和葡萄酒桶。共有 $*f*$ 个食品箱和 $*w*$ 个葡萄酒桶。Tarly 将它们存放在若干个堆中，每个堆只能由食品箱或葡萄酒桶组成，不能同时包含两者。这些堆排成一列，使得任意两个食品箱堆不相邻，任意两个葡萄酒桶堆也不相邻。

一个堆的高度定义为该堆中物品的数量。如果两个堆的高度不同，或者一个堆包含食品箱而另一个堆包含葡萄酒桶，则认为这两个堆不同。

如果任何一个葡萄酒桶堆的高度小于等于 $*h*$，Jon Snow 就不喜欢这种排列。当所有排列等概率出现时，Jon Snow 喜欢这种排列的概率是多少？

如果存在某个 $*i*$，使得一种排列中的第 $*i*$ 个堆与另一种排列中的第 $*i*$ 个堆不同，则认为这两种堆排列不同。

## 输入格式

输入的第一行包含三个整数 $*f*$、$*w*$、$*h*$（$0 ≤ *f*, *w*, *h* ≤ 10^{5}$），分别表示食品箱数量、葡萄酒桶数量以及上述定义中的 $*h*$。保证至少有一个食品箱或至少有一个葡萄酒桶。

## 输出格式

输出 Jon Snow 喜欢这种排列的概率。该概率的形式为 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/cb0172a656698061aefa8eb30b2dbcd1e31f508e.png)，因此你需要输出一个整数 $*p*·*q*^{ - 1} *mod* (10^{9} + 7)$。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，$*f*  =  1$、$*w*  =  1$ 且 $*h*  =  1$，只有两种可能的堆排列，Jon Snow 不喜欢其中任何一种。

在第二个样例中，$*f* =  1$、$*w* =  2$ 且 $*h* =  1$，共有三种排列。Jon Snow 喜欢其中的第 (1) 和第 (3) 种排列。因此概率为 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/14b21b617fcd2e25700376368355f7bbf975d8de.png)。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/ace4ab85ebe9626a851b3d4270a7dd7ed4b241c5.png)
